correctness.rationale: The site rule is a homomorphism on the finite product by using configurations supported on its memory sites. The coordinate homomorphisms are uniquely determined and have commuting images. The only possible kernels in S3 are trivial, A3, and S3. An automorphism coordinate excludes every other nontrivial coordinate by the trivial center; otherwise nontrivial coordinates factor by sign into the same order-two subgroup, since different transpositions do not commute. This gives both the unique normal forms and the allowed-memory count. Sign invariance and odd transpositions give the four products without a hidden sign or shift convention. The unit subgroup and nonunit ideal follow, and the center, five idempotents and regularity follow by conjugation of transpositions and cancellation in the Laurent domain (regularity requires a Laurent inverse). Alphabet automorphisms have finite order, so a power of each automorphism-shift is a pure shift of the corresponding length. For a nonzero polynomial the binary output equation can be solved in both directions using its two extreme coefficients, or directly for a monomial; the image is the full binary subgroup shift. Restriction to that first image does not change temporal entropy. The inspected scalar entropy theorem on this bilateral binary image gives the support span after including exponent zero. The claimed spectra are realized by monomials and shifts, with disjoint positive branches by prime factorization.
